summary:
The Monkey D. Luffy alternate art from Romance Dawn (OP01-003) is the card the modern One Piece Card Game collector market was built on. Romance Dawn borrows its name from the Eiichiro Oda one-shot that became One Piece itself, and OP01 was the block that introduced the game to the world - so the alternate-art Luffy inside it carries the double weight of being both the franchise's front man and the first set's headline chase. Every later Luffy parallel is measured against this one, which is why it behaves less like a single card and more like the benchmark the rest of the market quotes itself against.

### Basic Info
*   **Main subject / card theme:** Monkey D. Luffy, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates
*   **Set or product (catalog label):** 2022 Romance Dawn Alternate Art
*   **Card number:** OP01-003
*   **Language version(s):** English catalog entry; the Romance Dawn block was published in Japanese before its English release
*   **Rarity / treatment:** Alternate art parallel
*   **Set label year:** 2022

### Community Pulse
Conversation around this card is dominated by print-run forensics rather than by the artwork. Romance Dawn was reprinted repeatedly once demand for the game outran Bandai's initial expectations, and collectors separate the earliest run from later ones by inspecting the foil pattern and the way the holo treatment carries colour. That distinction is the single most argued-about detail in One Piece TCG collecting, and it means two copies sharing the same card number and the same grade are not automatically treated as the same asset. Beyond print runs, the usual condition anxieties apply: Bandai stock of this era has a reputation for centering drift and for edge wear that survives careful handling, so raw copies get picked over closely before anyone commits to grading fees. The card also works as a gateway piece - many collectors describe it as the first One Piece card they chased seriously, which keeps a layer of sentimental demand underneath the speculative one.

### Card Fun Facts
*   Romance Dawn takes its name from Oda's pre-serialisation one-shot, making OP01 a deliberate nod to the manga's own origin story rather than a generic launch-set title.
*   The alternate-art treatment reframes Luffy outside the standard card border, which is why this printing is so often displayed face-out instead of sleeved in a binder.
*   Because OP01 was reprinted while the game was still scaling, supply here is not one fixed population but a layered one, and the market prices those layers differently.

### Summary (TLDR)
OP01-003 alternate-art Luffy is the founding chase card of the One Piece Card Game: first main block, franchise lead character, and the printing every later Luffy parallel is benchmarked against. Its market is unusually sensitive to print-run identification and to condition, so the print layer and the grade matter at least as much as the card number.
